summary: This is a well-executed, fully archived preregistered paired study whose principal confirmatory comparison is uninformative because the verifier detected zero violations across all paired tasks (ceiling effect). The manuscript transparently reports that outcome and provides rich artifact-level reproducibility evidence. Major revisions are required to ensure claims and statistical statements are properly bounded, to explicitly document key execution details (shared-initial generation and validator acceptance predicates) within the five-page paper, and to include an explicit evidence-to-claim mapping so readers can verify each principal statement against archived artifacts.
critical_issues: Primary confirmatory claim cannot be tested in the executed regime: zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0) makes the preregistered McNemar comparison degenerate and prevents inference about verifier benefit.
Manuscript currently risks overinterpretation: some language implies an evaluation of verifier effectiveness when the experiment produced a ceiling effect that precludes that conclusion.

Insufficient explicit in-text documentation of two pivotal, run-determinative items that are critical for interpreting results and reproducibility: (a) the shared_initial generation policy produced identical generated candidates across baseline and guarded conditions (evidence: identical response file hashes in the execution manifest); (b) the full, exact validator acceptance predicates and configuration parameters used by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 are not presented inline (only referenced as archived files). Readers cannot fully assess whether the ceiling arose from generator behavior, overly permissive validator predicates, or both.

Statistical reporting needs correction and clearer interpretation: reporting McNemar p=1.0 without stating that the test is degenerate given zero discordant pairs is misleading; the manuscript must present the null informative consequence (untestable) rather than an implied negative result.

Evidence-to-claim traceability is incomplete within the five-page manuscript: key claims (e.g., counts, hashes, validator fields) should be explicitly mapped to specific archived artifact files/sha256 entries in a concise table or paragraph so reviewers/readers can verify assertions without external searching.
required_revisions: Explicitly state, in the Abstract and Methods (and where results are summarized), that the shared_initial generation policy produced the same candidate output for the paired baseline and guarded pipelines for every task; cite the representative response-file hashes (execution/responses/task-*-*.txt) and provide a concise summary (e.g., percentage of tasks with identical per-condition response hashes = 100%). This is verifiable from the supplied execution artifact hashes.

Replace or augment the current statistical wording to make clear that the preregistered McNemar comparison is degenerate/uninformative because n10=n01=0; explicitly state the inferential consequence (untestable under observed data) and remove any phrasing that could be read as evidence that the verifier had no effect in general.

Inline within the manuscript (Methods or an Appendix-style boxed paragraph that still fits pages 1–5) include the exact validator acceptance predicates and configuration parameters used by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (or a short excerpt) as archived in execution/model_configuration.json and representative scoring JSONs, and point to their sha256 hashes. If space is constrained, add a one-paragraph precise summary (field names and semantics) and cite artifact paths and hashes for full details.

Add an explicit evidence-to-claim table (concise, 3–6 rows) in the manuscript that maps every principal claim (preregistration timestamp and SHA, episode counts, per-pipeline valid-config counts, contingency table entries, contamination summary, model identity, shared_initial policy, verifier id) to the exact archived artifact file path(s) and sha256 values already present in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts.

Temper the paper’s contribution statements and conclusion: reframe the principal contribution as a reproducible methodological lesson and artifact release (i.e., that in this synthetic single-model/single-validator regime a ceiling effect occurred), and remove any wording that could be interpreted as a general evaluation of verifier utility or as a negative empirical verdict on verifiers more broadly. Cross-check nearest-work comparisons and remove any unverified 'first' or broad generality claims.
optional_revisions: If space permits, include a one-paragraph run-level summary that quantifies prompt-sensitivity checks or shows a small representative diff of generation attempts (even if only demonstrating identical outputs), using supplied provider_call or call_cache artifacts to illustrate generator determinism under the frozen prompt.
Add a short, concrete reproducibility checklist (steps, filenames, seeds) for readers to re-run verification of the key artifact pointers; cite exact JSONL line numbers or hashes where helpful.

In Related Work, add brief explicit contrast to recent multi-verifier or adversarial-task studies (if verifiable) to further motivate the recommended follow-ups; ensure each added citation is present in the verified-bibliography record.
